newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bank stocks up on S&P favourable ratings.
newsitem.headline: Manila bank stocks up on S&P favourable ratings.

text.p: The Bank of the Philippine Islands and Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co Inc rose by midsession on Wednesday following favourable ratings released by Standard & Poor's Corp, analysts said.
BPI rose eight pesos, or 5.48 percent, to 154 pesos while Metrobank rose five pesos, or 0.84 percent, to 600 pesos.
On Tuesday, S&P gave BPI a triple B rating while Metrobank was given a double B rating.
"It's because of the S&P ratings. It said the banking system has a very good capital risk ratio and a fairly good lending portfolio," Joy Quintos, research head of PrimeEast Securities said.
The Philippine National Bank, which suffered from massive selldown recently due to poor nine-month results, was still down by 7.50 pesos at 325 pesos. S&P gave PNB a double B rating.
